rationale: The telemetry from the last iteration shows the robot still fails to complete the tracks, with one line loss event per run and off-track termination around 10% progress. The increased wheel track to 0.18 and moving the rear sensors further back to y = -0.03 have not yet eliminated early line loss or off-track failures, though the maximum error and RMS error remain low, indicating good control when on track. The controller must compensate for the wider wheel track by slightly increasing steering gains to maintain responsiveness. I increased base_speed slightly to 0.15 to improve progress without risking stability. I increased kp to 0.22 and kd to 0.045 to enhance steering responsiveness and damping, helping the robot react more quickly to line deviations detected earlier by the rear sensors. I kept ki at 0.025 to maintain integral correction without causing oscillations. Sensor weights are adjusted to slightly reduce negative weights on rear sensors to -0.2 from -0.25, to balance their influence and avoid oversteering from early turn detection. The line_loss strategy remains 'search_left' as it suits the track and controller behavior. Observation request includes all previously requested measurements plus 'steering_oscillation' and 'control_effort' to monitor controller stability and effort in future races. These changes aim to leverage the improved geometry for earlier turn detection and better lateral stability, improving completion rates and reducing line loss events.
